Seminar Title:

Thermal Performance Characterization of Brick Wall Systems for Energy-Efficient Buildings: Experimental Investigation and Numerical Modelling

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Mechanical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Durga Prasad Vishwakarma ( Rollno : 524me1017)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

ME-001 (Seminar Room)

Date and Time:

28 Oct 2026 4:30 PM

Contact:

Sushil Kumar Rathore

Abstract:

The hygrothermal behaviour of building envelope materials influences indoor thermal comfort and building energy consumption, particularly across diverse climatic conditions. This study investigates the thermal and moisture responses of autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC) blocks, concrete bricks, and solid clay bricks using the combined heat and moisture transfer finite-element (HAMT) model in EnergyPlus v25.2.0. Identical room models were evaluated under free-floating and conditioned operating conditions for five Indian cities: Mumbai, New Delhi, Jaipur, Bangalore, and Srinagar. Summer and winter performance was assessed using temperature decrement factor, time lag, relative-humidity attenuation ratio, and RH peak lag, while conditioned performance was evaluated in terms of annual HVAC thermal energy demand (ideal-loads basis) and peak loads. Under free-floating conditions, concrete brick consistently exhibited the lowest temperature decrement factor, followed by solid clay brick and AAC, indicating stronger attenuation of indoor temperature fluctuations. However, AAC maintained higher indoor temperatures during winter, with an advantage of up to 1.7&ndash1.8 &degC in Srinagar. The influence of wall material on indoor RH was comparatively small. Under conditioned operation, AAC achieved the lowest annual HVAC energy demand in New Delhi (19,201 kWh), Jaipur (17,912 kWh), Bangalore (16,662 kWh), and Srinagar (43,223 kWh), corresponding to savings of approximately 12.6&ndash13.8%, 11.5&ndash12.6%, 8.8&ndash9.7%, and 18.9&ndash20.5%, respectively, relative to the two brick alternatives. In Mumbai, the three wall systems showed comparatively small differences in annual energy consumption, with concrete brick performing best. These findings demonstrate that wall-material selection should consider both climatic conditions and building operation. Higher thermal mass favours damping of temperature fluctuations, whereas the lower thermal transmittance of AAC can reduce HVAC energy demand in most of the studied climates.
